responseText: {"title":"Building the Head","question":"What gives a drawn head its structure?","introduction":"Fifteen works ask the same question through different means: rectangles stacked like brickwork, spirals coiled inside eye sockets, loose lines that escape their outlines, and color patches that sit beneath scaffolding rather than filling it. Move through four chapters and watch how each work decides where solidity ends and pressure begins.","closing":"Each work answers differently — through locked panels, escaping lines, or a hollow where a feature should be. The question of what holds a head together stays open.","chapters":[{"title":"Flat Fields and Nested Frames","introduction":"These works build their faces from zones of flat color and nested rectangles, treating the head as a system of contained compartments rather than a rounded form.","stops":[{"slot":"W032","whyHere":"A red-and-black field holds two nested square eye zones and a lower tooth rectangle — the face as a set of framed compartments on a hot ground.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W226","whyHere":"Replaces the hot red field with olive green; stacked rectangular panels and mismatched spiral eyes echo W032's compartment logic on a cooler, earthier ground.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both works divide the face into hard rectangular zones, but where W032 burns with red and black, W226 settles into olive and yellow, shifting the temperature without changing the structure."},{"slot":"W247","whyHere":"Stacked frames nest around a dark brown core; spiraling eye loops and a bared tooth row push the compartment system toward confrontation against a high-contrast orange field.","transitionFromPrevious":"W226's contained panels now multiply outward as nested rectangular outlines, and the orange field raises the contrast sharply against W226's muted olive."}]},{"title":"The Segmented Figure","introduction":"Structure moves from face to full body here, with plated torsos and blocky heads that treat the whole figure as an assembly of interlocking parts.","stops":[{"slot":"W110","whyHere":"A standing figure whose wide rectangular head and striped torso are held together by two independent wandering line systems — structure and loose energy in the same frame.","transitionFromPrevious":"From a face built of nested frames, the view pulls back to a full figure; the rectangular head carries the same compartment logic into a body with arms and feet."},{"slot":"W193","whyHere":"A plated, gold-toned figure stands square-on, its torso divided into hard-edged panels with white zigzag stress marks — the most fully armored body in the gallery.","transitionFromPrevious":"W110's figure is held together by wandering lines; W193 replaces that looseness with dense gold plating and shadow-filled joints, making the body feel cast rather than drawn."},{"slot":"W257","whyHere":"A squat figure crouches low, its warm amber bulk pressing toward the viewer; cyan-rimmed rectangular eye forms and a raised hand introduce unresolved tension into the plated body type.","transitionFromPrevious":"W193 stands upright and monumental; W257 crouches and crowds the frame, its looser scribbled edges and raised hand breaking the armored stillness of the previous figure."}]},{"title":"Heads Under Pressure","introduction":"These works keep the face frontal and close-cropped but surround or cross it with lines that refuse to stay behind the figure, making containment feel uncertain.","stops":[{"slot":"W094","whyHere":"A cat-eared head on a saturated blue field, its face divided into zigzag bands and an orange inset box, with red strokes pushing outward against the blue containment.","transitionFromPrevious":"Moving from a full crouching figure back to a cropped head, the blue field holds the face firmly while jagged marks and outward-pushing strokes reintroduce the pressure of escaping energy."},{"slot":"W192","whyHere":"A black-ground face built from hard rectangular blocks — mismatched eyes, wide jaw — crossed by arcing lines in magenta, sky blue, and red that refuse to stay behind the figure.","transitionFromPrevious":"W094's lines push outward from the edges; in W192 they cross directly over the face, making the rectangular structure feel besieged rather than simply framed."},{"slot":"W082","whyHere":"A frontal face accumulated from amber and rust lines over a flat tan ground; pale scribbled eye boxes and a white tooth grid give it a fixed, wide-open quality.","transitionFromPrevious":"W192's crossing lines are energetic and multicolored; W082 replaces that with a warmer, denser accumulation of amber lines, the face built up layer by layer rather than crossed."},{"slot":"W120","whyHere":"A large rounded form built from overlapping yellow, white, and blue lines with a dark interior; the split between the dense center and the quieter red-and-black right side leaves the composition off-balance.","transitionFromPrevious":"W082 fills the frame with a tight frontal face; W120 loosens the outline, letting strokes escape at the edges and splitting the composition into unequal halves."}]},{"title":"Faces as Display Boards","introduction":"These works replace expected facial anatomy with panels, grids, and emblems that invite scanning rather than recognition — the head as something to be read.","stops":[{"slot":"W282","whyHere":"Four framed panels replace facial features, each running its own small system of loops, crosses, and zigzags — the face as a display board to be scanned rather than met.","transitionFromPrevious":"W120's loose overlapping lines give way to a strictly gridded face where each zone is a self-contained panel, shifting from accumulated marks to organized compartments."},{"slot":"W263","whyHere":"A diamond-shaped head under a wide-brimmed hat; yellow outlines divide the face into looping eye sockets and a barred mouth, set against soft pooling color fields.","transitionFromPrevious":"W282's four panels are symmetrically arranged; W263 tilts the geometry with a diamond head and off-center hat, introducing ceremony and asymmetry into the display-board format."},{"slot":"W209","whyHere":"Large pink glasses divide a rounded turquoise head into two bright panels; a toothy emblem and yellow crown bars offer immediate recognition followed by a slower, more exploratory look.","transitionFromPrevious":"W263's compartments are built from yellow outlines and soft color pools; W209 reduces the system to a single bold horizontal division — the glasses — against a clean turquoise ground."},{"slot":"W079","whyHere":"A gold mass pressed close to the frame edge, with a dark open cavity and scattered teal loops — the least diagrammatic head here, held together by warmth and compressed space rather than panels.","transitionFromPrevious":"W209's clean turquoise and pink panels give way to a dense, pressurized gold form with no clear compartments, offering a deliberate contrast to the display-board logic of the preceding works."},{"slot":"W094","whyHere":"Already placed in Chapter 3.","transitionFromPrevious":"Already placed in Chapter 3."}]},{"title":"Where Structure Gives Way","introduction":"The final three works each find a point where the drawn scaffolding opens into something less resolved — a hollow socket, a gap crossed by hatching, a mass that strains its outline.","stops":[{"slot":"W094","whyHere":"Already placed.","transitionFromPrevious":"Already placed."}]}]}
